summary: Former apartheid police dog handler Louis van Schoor became a security guard in East London, South Africa, and shot over a hundred mostly poor Black people in the late 1980s, killing at least 39 with police cover.

evidence.note: born in 1951, possibly in East London
background segment on Dutch colonisation, Van Riebeeck's hedge and the Boer wars
Section 49 lets police and security guards lawfully kill fleeing suspects
drops out at 16 to join the police and becomes a dog-unit handler
refused re-entry to the police, he joins Falcon Security run by an ex-police major
1988 shooting of a 14-year-old boy who is then charged with breaking in
bulk of the killings placed around 1986 to 1989
local reporters and Black Sash expose him despite sub judice rules and editors
inquest into a Wimpy bar shooting where a 13-year-old was killed
1989 inquiry, 1991 arrest; convicted of seven of 39 killings
daughter Sabrina has her mother murdered; 2002 trial
released after about 12 years, farm controversy, dies July 2024

notes: main_span ends 1992 for his conviction; the transcript gives the 1991 arrest but not the conviction year, which comes from general knowledge. Start 1986 is approximate (host thinks killings began earlier at Falcon). The colonial history segment is background for themes only, not counted in covered_span. No theme for serial killers; policing-incarceration plus criminal-killer carry it. Sabrina's end year null as her status is not stated.
